title: Trajeglish: Traffic Modeling as Next-Token Prediction

control_signal.value: Map, initial agent states (position, heading, size, class), and, in partial-control use, actions already chosen by other agents including replayed agents; no behaviour-style controls in packet.

control_mechanism.value: Autoregressive conditioning: each agent's next motion token is predicted given the encoded map and initial states, previous actions, and actions of agents earlier in the same timestep (agent order).

base_model.value: GPT-like encoder-decoder transformer over discrete motion tokens (k-disks tokenization, vocabulary 384), VectorNet map encoder with latent query attention, trained with next-token cross-entropy.

datasets.value: Waymo Open Motion Dataset (training, Sim Agents Benchmark); nuScenes used for transfer/fine-tuning.

metrics.value: WOMD Sim Agents metrics: realism meta, kinematic, interactive, map-based, minADE; partial-control collision rate; negative log-likelihood for context-length and scaling analyses.

controllability_evidence.value: Partial control: collision rate drops significantly when the controlled agent acts last in the order (no number given). Benchmark: realism meta 0.5339 versus 0.5168 for the next-best listed model.

notes: Imitative sim-agent model, not really controllable generation; packet shows only partial-control (replay) setting. LoRA gave too little expressiveness for nuScenes transfer (p9) but is a finding, not a stated limitation.
